proof.label: Sample

reviews.name: Cormac D.
reviews.text: Bram looked at our brick side wall in Fair Haven in March and said wait until May for the nights to warm up. He was right. Two winters on, the colors are still sharp and nothing has flaked.

reviews.name: Philomena G.
reviews.text: A snowy week in January, and they painted the whole stair wall with East Rock at sunset. Quiet, tidy, gone by four every day.

reviews.name: Arjun V.
reviews.text: The board fence by the shore gets salt spray every storm. They scraped it, primed it with something meant for that, and painted a row of sailboats. It still looks fresh after a nor'easter.

reviews.name: Rosalind K.
reviews.text: Gold leaf on the window of our little bookshop. People stop and touch the glass. Worth waiting for the warm week to do it.

reviews.name: Stellan J.
reviews.text: Our pizza place is closed Mondays and Tuesdays, so they painted the back room on those two days for three weeks. Never smelled paint during service once.

reviews.name: Margit T.
reviews.text: Our neighborhood mural on the old hardware store had lost half its color to sun and salt. They repaired the mortar spots first, matched the faded colors, and resealed it in June.

proof.guarantee: Any chip or peel on our outdoor work, we touch up free for three winters after the wall is done.
